samples.question: The image is a dense 32-by-32 lattice of bright and dark cells that looks like pure noise, but the noise is exactly symmetric about the main diagonal (subtracting the transposed copy cancels the noise). A coarse diagonal-band glyph was written as an anti-symmetric brightness bias. Take the field and subtract its transpose (reflect across the main diagonal, swapping rows and columns); the surviving field is a clean single diagonal band. Which band is revealed, A or B? Answer A or B.
